lark_e07_entry.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry.text: On Day Fifty Five, the fifth pair began as a line Lin could not complete. Duan placed a plain diagram beside the stopped board and asked her to identify the two ends without sending qi between them. The exercise seemed simple until she named an end by the direction it appeared to point. He turned the diagram around. Her answer turned with it. The route in her body had not moved. She put down the pointer and began again using the fixed primary trunk references the received curriculum actually named.

lark_e07_entry_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_002.text: Duan did not supply the answer while she was looking. He watched her touch the diagram's first reference, then stop before reaching the second. Lin could feel the place she expected the connection to go, and that expectation was easier to follow than the printed reference. She said so. Duan shifted his chair to rest the knee and told her to keep those two things separate for one morning. An expected path might help her search. It could also make her overlook the path she was actually preparing to test.

lark_e07_entry_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_003.text: The first formal instruction of the practice week remained seated and unpowered. Lin marked the route from each end in turn. The two marks failed to meet by the width of her own careless thumb. She blamed the scale until Duan gave her a larger clean diagram. The same mismatch appeared. She had used a different reference when approaching from the second end. Correcting it made both lines meet on paper. The fifth pair itself was still unopened. A drawing had caught one false intention before her body paid for it.

lark_e07_entry_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_004.text: The paper task tired her differently from a work shift. There was no load, no ringing apparatus, and no reader waiting on the stair. Yet she kept noticing where her shoulder wanted to lean forward as if strain would make the route clearer. Duan had her rest the forearm on the low support and name the ordinary muscle tension. It belonged in the account even though it was not qi. The curriculum would be less useful if every uncomfortable sensation could disguise itself as proof that a new pair was stirring.

lark_e07_entry_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_005.text: At the received end of the meeting, Duan accepted its four copper fee. Two formal meetings had now occurred, and eighteen remained in the eighty copper scope. Lin kept the diagram in the local practice folder with its two failed marks still visible. She had permission to use that curriculum sheet here, not an impulse to improve its appearance for later praise. Jiang closed the apparatus room after checking that no powered work had been attempted. The stopped board had supplied a place to learn without becoming the cause of a false success.

lark_e07_entry_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_006.text: Lin took her midday bowl outside. Qin Yi was sitting on the low wall, moving a chestnut between three cups with such obvious delight that losing to her seemed unavoidable. Lin chose the wrong cup. The child revealed the chestnut in her hand and called it a new method. Lin asked whether the method included permission to move the chestnut off the table. Qin Yi said nobody had forbidden it. Shan Fang, passing with a basket, told her to explain that rule before charging a second chestnut. The game became less profitable and more interesting.

lark_e07_entry_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_007.text: The child was preparing a small performance for the market's late week gathering. The scene involved a carrier, a foolish goat, and an examiner who could not find his shoe. Duan had unknowingly supplied the third character. Qin Yi wanted the shrine room for rehearsal because its window made the paper animals bright. Shan Fang had agreed to ask the keeper. The room was a shared place now, and asking was different from setting the animals on every stool until the mending people surrendered their seats.

lark_e07_entry_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_008.text: Lin's independent diagram practice also needed a quiet table on the afternoon of Day Fifty Seven. The lodging common room would hold a paid merchant meeting, and Duan's room would be unavailable while the landlord repaired its drain. The shrine keeper could reserve the window table for her practice or let Qin Yi rehearse with two other children. There was an alternative dim corner for Lin at the lower desk and an exposed landing for the children, but both alternatives had real limits. Somebody would get the better room and somebody would adapt.

lark_e07_entry_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_009.text: Shan Fang did not ask Lin to call the rehearsal more important than practice. She wanted to know whether Lin needed the window, because she did not want her daughter's performance to become a small tyranny fed by adult politeness. The shrine keeper waited with his reservation book. Lin knew the lower desk would allow only a shorter session before its ordinary readers arrived. The children knew the landing might be too windy for their paper scenery. Neither inconvenience was fatal, and neither would disappear if everybody pretended not to mind.

lark_e07_entry_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_entry_010.text: Lin visited both alternatives before answering. The lower desk's lamp could light the diagram clearly if the keeper accepted the oil use and cleared one stool for the offered hour. The exposed landing was spacious but turned every loose sheet toward the ravine. Qin Yi demonstrated with a scrap and lost it before finishing her complaint. Shan Fang retrieved the scrap from a safe lower step. The practical differences made the decision less abstract. Lin could keep the quiet bright table, or accept the shorter desk session and give the rehearsal its protected window.

lark_e07_room_choice.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_choice.text: The reservation book had one window table to offer on Day Fifty Seven. Lin's practice could use it for two quiet hours. Qin Yi's rehearsal could use it for the same afternoon. Keeping the table would protect Lin's longer session and send the paper scenery outside; yielding would give the children a sheltered rehearsal and bind her own practice to the lower desk's shorter accepted hour. She chose which arrangement to make real.

choices.text: Keep the reserved window table for the full quiet practice.
Give the rehearsal the room and accept the shorter desk session.

lark_e07_room_practice.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_practice.text: Lin accepted the window table's two hour reservation. Shan Fang told the children they would rehearse on the landing only if the weather permitted, and that nobody had wronged them by needing the room first. Qin Yi took this instruction as a reason to dislike the weather in advance. Lin watched the keeper enter the reservation, then sent the lower desk a timely refusal before it prepared a lamp for her. She would not keep both places available so the first could be quietly exchanged if the afternoon proved inconvenient.

lark_e07_room_practice_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_practice_002.text: On Day Fifty Seven, Lin used the bright table for the agreed diagram practice. She repeated the references from both ends and found the fifth pair's intended line consistent on paper. The second hour let her compare three task orders without hurrying through the last. There was no teacher beside her and no authority for an unsupervised powered opening. She kept the work unpowered as planned. A reader passing the doorway asked whether it looked right. Lin said the formal received test was still ahead. The useful afternoon did not need a certificate hidden inside it.

lark_e07_room_practice_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_practice_003.text: Outside, the wind strengthened before the children reached their first full scene. Qin Yi weighted the paper goat with a little pebble and turned its head upside down. The other children laughed. A loose examiner's shoe escaped and fell onto a closed storage roof, where nobody could safely fetch it during rehearsal. Shan Fang ended the session at the agreed weather limit. The children carried the surviving scenery indoors afterward, with the lost shoe still lost. They would have to cut another one or alter the scene before the market performance.

lark_e07_room_practice_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_practice_004.text: Lin emerged when her reservation ended and saw Qin Yi holding the damaged goat. She did not offer to pretend the rehearsal had gone well. The child said the room should have belonged to everybody and therefore to her. Lin said everybody included the person practicing at its table. Shan Fang let the disagreement remain between them instead of making her daughter apologize for being disappointed. Lin offered the leftover plain paper from her own private stock for a new shoe. Qin Yi accepted the paper while declining, for now, to like the giver.

lark_e07_room_rehearsal.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_rehearsal.text: Lin gave up the shrine room reservation and accepted the lower desk's single lamp hour. The desk keeper named the ordinary readers' arrival time as its end, and Lin repeated it before agreeing. Shan Fang thanked her without promising that the child's performance would deserve the sacrifice. Qin Yi celebrated by making the paper goat bow so deeply its neck tore. Lin helped hold it while the child placed a repair behind the drawing. The bright room had been reserved for real people, not for an ideal rehearsal that could never make a mistake.

lark_e07_room_rehearsal_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_rehearsal_002.text: On Day Fifty Seven, the children rehearsed beside the sheltered window. Shan Fang sat near the door while they argued about whether a goat could be examined without permission. Their scenery stayed on the table, and they reached the scene's ending twice before the first child had to go home. Qin Yi cut the examiner's shoe too large, then chose to leave it that way because the joke improved. Lin did not watch the whole rehearsal. Her own accepted desk hour was elsewhere, and giving the room away had not made her practice optional.

lark_e07_room_rehearsal_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_rehearsal_003.text: The lower desk lamp lit her diagram well enough. She repeated the primary references from each end and kept the work unpowered under the accepted independent plan. The hour allowed two task orders, not the third she had hoped to compare. When the first ordinary reader arrived, she closed the folder on time. The keeper needed the stool for a person with a received appointment. Lin wrote the unfinished comparison on the next formal meeting's question list rather than claiming a hurried final glance had completed it. The choice had cost an actual piece of practice time.

lark_e07_room_rehearsal_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_room_rehearsal_004.text: At evening, Qin Yi brought her the repaired goat and performed the first scene alone. The child used the oversized shoe as evidence that grown people had measured it badly. Lin laughed and asked whether the goat was still foolish. Qin Yi said the goat was the only one who knew what a foot looked like. The protected rehearsal had produced a more complete scene and a pleased child. Lin still had one task order to examine under Duan's next meeting. She could welcome the gift and carry the missing work honestly.

lark_e07_after_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_001.text: The next formal meeting began on Day Fifty Eight with the independent diagram folder open between Lin and Duan. He asked what she had actually completed on the free afternoon and what remained. She showed the marks in their dated order. Whatever room she had used, the new powered task would need its own received preparation. Duan checked the references she had drawn and asked her to identify the last task order without looking. She found one place where memory had replaced the fixed reference with a direction. They corrected it before touching the stopped board.

lark_e07_after_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_002.text: The first fifth pair attempt used a smaller registered input than the familiar fourth pair task. Duan did not ask her to expand the old duration, range, or breath ceiling to compensate for uncertainty. Lin began where the primary trunk diagram placed the first end. The sensation she had expected did not arrive. A different warmth gathered higher, close to the place her shoulder had been holding tension. She wanted it to mean a new connection. She released the effort and reported the warmth's actual position instead.

lark_e07_after_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_003.text: Jiang checked the board while Duan asked her to describe how the sensation changed after stopping. The warmth faded with the ordinary tension in her shoulder, before the comparison strip showed a useful new task. It could not serve as evidence that the fifth pair had opened. Lin felt cheated by her own expectation, which was a feeling she had no technical reason to defend. Duan let her be disappointed. He asked for the starting references again only after the disappointment had stopped pulling her hand toward another immediate attempt.

lark_e07_after_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_004.text: They used an unpowered movement to check her posture. A stool placed slightly too far back made her lean into the board, and the recovering shoulder joined an effort that did not require it. Lin had arranged the stool carefully at lodging and still placed this one badly in the practice room. The two stools were different heights. She could have turned the error into a reason to distrust every diagram. Duan instead asked her to measure the ordinary distance between seat and support. The correction belonged to furniture before it belonged to channels.

lark_e07_after_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_005.text: On the second accepted attempt, she used the fixed references and the changed stool position. A faint connection appeared along the intended primary line, then broke when she shifted her attention to whether Duan had seen it. She stopped within the agreed task. The useful output did not reach the criterion for even this small practice. Duan marked it as an interrupted fifth pair attempt. He did not call it nothing. Something had happened at the intended place. He also did not call it a stable route merely because its beginning had been correctly located.

lark_e07_after_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_006.text: Lin asked whether the interrupted connection should change her stage description. Duan asked what the existing certificate said. Four stable primary pairs under recovered fifth stage checks. The new task had not yet added a stable fifth pair, much less the sixth and all the later independent examinations. Her current description stayed where the work supported it. Lin knew that answer already, which did not spare her the wish to ask. Duan said many useful questions were asked twice: once for knowledge and once because the speaker finally needed to live with the answer.

lark_e07_after_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_007.text: After the registered stop and ordinary rest, the pair's faint beginning no longer felt like a promise. It felt like a place that had accepted one careful visit and rejected haste. Lin wrote the task's input and actual duration beside the interruption, without a story about latent potential. Jiang received the apparatus condition as ordinary and closed the board. Duan's third formal meeting fee of four copper was paid for instruction performed. He had guided an interrupted attempt, not sold her a completed pair. Lin would return under the next accepted plan after recovery.

lark_e07_after_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_008.text: Outside, a woman was searching for a goat that had pushed through a gate while the latch was being repaired. She had been given three confident sightings in incompatible directions. Lin asked which of them somebody had actually seen and learned that two were guesses based on where goats usually preferred to go. The woman pointed to the third witness, a child with a fresh muddy mark on one sleeve. The child had seen it pass the lower cabbage stall. Lin went that way with the owner along the currently open public route.

lark_e07_after_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_009.text: They found the goat beside an empty carrying basket, eating a handful of leaves that had fallen from a vendor's stock. The owner asked the vendor before entering the stall's working space. He wanted the goat removed and his remaining leaves left alone. Lin held the gate of the stall's little fenced corner while the owner used its ordinary lead. She did not grab the animal's horns or ask a fifth pair to make up for a gate's position. The vendor put the fallen leaves in a bucket and watched the goat leave with visible regret.

lark_e07_after_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_010.text: The child who had supplied the useful sighting wanted to collect a reward that nobody had offered. The owner gave him a small leaf cake as a voluntary thanks after hearing his question. She also told him which gate he could knock at next time he saw an animal missing. Lin enjoyed the directness of the exchange. A child had performed a useful observation and asked plainly for a cake. He had not invented a larger story to make his help sound indispensable. The goat tried to eat the ordinary lead on the walk home.

lark_e07_after_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_011.text: The repaired latch waited in the owner's yard. Its maker had kept the old catch for comparison and showed where repeated use had worn the edge. The goat had exploited a real defect rather than vindicating somebody's belief that it was unusually clever. The owner accepted the new catch after closing and opening it from both sides. Lin kept the animal in the yard while the maker did that work. The child had already gone home with his cake. Every participant's useful part ended at a different place.

lark_e07_after_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_012.text: On her way back, Lin passed the public warning sheet from the supplier comparison. Whatever session she had chosen, the association's ordinary status notice remained available. No new signal fitting had been installed. She read the current date and left the page in place. The market's ordinary safety facts belonged to people walking its stair, not to those who had gained restricted access. Hu Lan had kept that boundary visible. It let a seller ask about the freight bell without becoming responsible for a private drawing or a client's future contract.

lark_e07_after_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_013.text: Qin came uphill with an empty cart at the end of his receiving. The axle's repaired wheel turned quietly. He had a letter from a relative who wanted to visit with two children and no clear return plan. Shan Fang was glad to see them, but the lodging space would not expand because everybody missed each other. Qin said he had written to ask how many nights the relative could pay for elsewhere if the household's spare pallet was not enough. Lin thought he sounded severe. Then he asked whether severity could be expressed with a drawing of a bed.

lark_e07_after_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_014.text: He did not want to disappoint the relative after the family had already reached the mountain. A clear answer now would be kinder than making Shan Fang feed an unexpected household while he remained cheerful about guests. Lin offered to help read the reply when it came, and he said he could read a letter well enough. What he wanted was somebody willing to tell him if he had sounded like a man refusing his own family. Lin read the draft when he brought it and found the spare pallet named warmly and plainly.

lark_e07_after_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_015.text: Qin revised one sentence that had asked the relative to be sensible. It became a question about the actual arrival date and the children's ages. The information would let Shan Fang decide what could fit. The letter was posted from Qin's own money. Lin did not become the household's correspondence keeper because she had read a page. She went back to her lodging with the pleasant unease of having said that an ordinary bed was finite. At her own door, she thanked the keeper for the room whose exact size she had begun to know.

lark_e07_after_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_016.text: Her accepted shift on Day Fifty Six had been received before the free afternoon, adding four copper to forty and leaving her at eleven completed shifts. She used one of her own earned copper that evening to buy a longer needle for the glove's thick seam. The seller would have sold her a carved case as well. Lin chose the needle alone and wrapped it in a spare fold of cloth. Qin Yi considered the absence of a case proof that adults could be disappointingly difficult to sell beautiful things to.

lark_e07_after_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_017.text: The shrine keeper wanted the mending room's lamp oil accounted for through the neighbors' actual shared contribution. He set the small jar beside the shelf with its weekly use mark. Somebody had left a taper burning after the last gathering, and the remaining oil would not last the expected week. Nobody confessed to being the last person in the room. The keeper did not demand a culprit before explaining the new closing check. The room could lose another evening while the people searched for a person to blame, or they could first stop the recurring empty lamp.

lark_e07_after_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_018.text: Shan Fang offered to do the check on the nights she already attended. Another woman accepted the alternate nights. Qin Yi volunteered for every night and was refused because she did not actually stay until closing. Lin accepted no standing duty, since her instruction and work dates changed across the term. She did help mark a place on the shelf for the turned down wick. The new arrangement named people who would truly be there. The keeper received it with fewer dramatic vows than the room's first opening had attracted.

lark_e07_after_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_019.text: The next morning, Duan asked Lin how she understood practice after an interrupted connection. She said she wanted to repeat the motion until it stopped feeling interrupted. He asked whether fatigue could make repetition teach her to accept a bad path as familiar. She disliked that possibility and could not dismiss it. They agreed on short unpowered reference work between supervised attempts, with the current ordinary rest plan preserved. There was no accepted instruction that persistence meant continuing every sensation. The fifth pair would have to become dependable under interruption, not merely recognizable through repetition.

lark_e07_after_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_020.text: Duan told her about a novice who had learned a sequence so thoroughly that an early mistake became part of its rhythm. He did not supply the novice's name. The correction had required slowing the practiced part until the learner could notice the bad reference again. Lin wondered if the novice had been him. He said the useful part of the story did not depend on that. She looked at the worn corner of his diagram and decided to let the question remain private. A teacher could offer a mistake without turning somebody's whole history into a classroom.

lark_e07_after_021.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_021.text: Lin used the next quiet hour to draw only the fixed references, leaving the connection between them blank. The absence made her impatient. She had wanted the new pair to be a line she could hold in her mind as if holding were equivalent to opening. Blank paper admitted the missing work more clearly. She folded it once and kept it separate from the successful route diagram. When the child at the lodging asked what the empty page showed, Lin said two places she was still learning to join.

lark_e07_after_022.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_022.text: The child offered to draw a bridge between them. Lin said the offer was kind but would answer a different question. He drew the bridge on his own scrap anyway and gave it to her. The bridge had tall rails and a fish under its middle. She put it above the wash basin, where an ordinary imaginary structure could be enjoyed without being mistaken for an instruction. The real fifth pair remained on the blanked diagram in her practice folder. The two papers did not need to compete for the same kind of truth.

lark_e07_after_023.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_023.text: On Day Fifty Nine, rain reached the pass in a slow grey sheet. Freight workers used the actual wet route plan, and the higher view closed before the wind made its notices difficult to read. Lin remained off shift and made no application to inspect a dangerous place in order to prove she cared. She watched water drip from the lodging eave into the public channel. A loose cabbage leaf lodged beneath the grate. The lodging keeper removed it with the ordinary hook while the flow was still shallow enough for the accepted task.

lark_e07_after_024.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_after_024.text: The rain had no convenient message for her new pair. It interrupted a merchant's visit, gave the shrine room a fuller crowd, and softened a page Qin Yi had left near the window. Shan Fang moved the paper scenery away from the damp sill. Lin brought her repaired glove and sat at the end of the room's low shelf. Nobody needed her to describe the weather as a trial sent for her progress. It was a wet day at a mountain market, and everybody had work whose size had just changed.

lark_e07_late_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_001.text: At the lower stall, a widow was trying to collect payment for a load of woven basket liners. The buyer said the rain had made them too damp to receive. She said his promised covered space had been unavailable at the accepted time. Lin could hear the dispute from the mending room's doorway and went no farther until the widow asked her to read the order. The order named that space and time. The buyer's wish to postpone receiving was new. It did not by itself cancel what he had offered her.

lark_e07_late_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_002.text: The buyer had used the covered space for a visiting supplier's crates. He could no longer make it available on the original date. His explanation was practical and his inconvenience real. So was the widow's afternoon spent bringing the liners uphill. The market keeper came when both parties accepted him as their ordinary receiver for a revised arrangement. Lin read the original terms once, then stopped speaking while the keeper asked which present space could actually protect the stock. She was not the person empowered to settle the price by being loudest about fairness.

lark_e07_late_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_003.text: The buyer offered a dry corner in his inner room if the liners could be counted there. The widow would not let her entire stock disappear into a room she could not see. They agreed to move one bundle at a time, count and receive it beside the doorway, and place it on the named dry rack before the next bundle entered. The buyer paid the completed receiving price for each bundle. His original space failure remained on the revised record. The widow got her work paid without being told to trust a closed door.

lark_e07_late_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_004.text: Lin carried only the light order sheet. Qin, whose freight work had ended, declined an unpriced request to haul every bundle as a favor to the buyer. The widow then offered him a separate short move at a price he accepted, paid from the buyer's agreed extra handling allowance. The task did not happen because Lin had asked a friend to be useful. Qin inspected the rack's approach and completed the accepted move. He received the named pay before taking his cart home. The widow laughed for the first time since the rain began.

lark_e07_late_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_005.text: At supper, Qin said he would have moved one bundle voluntarily if the widow had needed it. What irritated him was the buyer assuming he could owe an entire job because he already stood near a cart. Shan Fang said he was also irritated that the buyer called him brother while forgetting his name. Qin admitted this was part of it. Lin remembered how readily she herself turned a familiar person's presence into an available solution in her thoughts. The man who had a cart also had a child, supper, and a tired back.

lark_e07_late_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_006.text: The rain cleared during the night. On Day Sixty, Lin completed her twelfth accepted ordinary shift in the posted role. The receiving keeper paid its four copper, bringing total wages to forty eight. The fifth received meal and lodging week had begun under the accepted five copper provision, making twenty five received in that category. At the day's end she was tired enough that the diagram's fixed references looked interchangeable. She closed the folder instead of teaching herself that tired mistake. Tomorrow's formal lesson would need the rested mind she could prepare tonight.

lark_e07_late_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_007.text: She walked the lower loop slowly after supper, inside the clinician's ordinary movement plan. A patch of wet stone made her shorten the turn. Her established lower limb pairs were not used to override a doubtful foot placement. She had ordinary shoes on an ordinary public stair, with no prepared reinforcement task or inspected conducting stitch offered for this walk. The body that had earned four pairs could still slip. She kept one hand near the rail without hanging her recovering shoulder from it and reached the lodging in less dramatic fashion.

lark_e07_late_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_008.text: The window's latch had swollen in the rain. Lin asked the lodging keeper before trimming its wooden edge or forcing it shut. He brought a small plane and checked the fit himself. A guest in the next room urged him to shave away more, predicting that dry weather would swell it again. The keeper said dry weather would do the opposite to this wood. The guest insisted he had meant another season. Lin held the lantern at a useful angle and left the explanation to the person who would remain responsible for the window.

lark_e07_late_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_009.text: The plane made a thin curled shaving that looked like a pale ribbon. Qin Yi collected it next morning for the paper goat's beard. Lin checked that the tool had been put away before letting her reach beneath the sill. The child wanted to glue the shaving immediately but had no paste. She considered wet millet, rejected it as a risk to the room's mice, and asked Shan Fang for the permitted craft jar. The goat acquired a beard through three ordinary questions. Its audience would probably not hear about any of them.

lark_e07_late_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_010.text: Duan's fourth formal meeting began on Day Sixty One. His knee was swollen enough that he used only the seated task he could currently support. He did not demonstrate six pairs to preserve his authority. The accepted curriculum included a stopped diagram comparison and low board instruction, both of which he could perform within his present limits. Lin asked whether he needed a different chair. He did, and the keeper brought it. The accommodation cost ten minutes and prevented a day of pointless suffering disguised as a teacher's dignity.

lark_e07_late_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_011.text: Lin showed him the independent work's blank connection line. Duan recognized what she had been trying to separate and asked her to add the intended path from fixed references under three changed orientations. This time the marks met. He turned the board's task order around without turning the primary anatomy into a different route. Lin could explain the corresponding start and stop without making the direction on the paper do the work. Duan received that preparation and allowed a new small attempt inside the currently accepted ceiling.

lark_e07_late_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_012.text: The fifth pair carried a faint permitted trace longer than it had at the earlier attempt. The first interruption succeeded. The second planned movement did not complete its useful task. Lin stopped there rather than borrowing extra input from the apparent success of the first. Jiang's apparatus record showed the same limitation from the external side. Neither observer called the whole attempt a qualification. A particular part had become more repeatable, and a different part still failed. The pair was a developing practice route, while the six pair certificate remained many required tests away.

lark_e07_late_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_013.text: Duan asked Lin to describe the useful improvement without using the phrase nearly complete. She named the first controlled interruption and the fixed starting reference. He asked her to describe the missing work with the same precision. She named the second movement's incomplete useful result. The two statements could sit beside each other without one cancelling the other. Lin realized how often nearly had allowed her to move between pride and disappointment while avoiding the place where the next work truly belonged. Today that place could be named on an ordinary page.

lark_e07_late_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_014.text: Her established reserve was checked after the registered sampling and rest rather than counted from the highest earlier reading. The day did not extend her recovered throughput beyond the old primary task ceiling. Jiang received the apparatus condition and closed the practice task. Four copper paid Duan for the fourth formal meeting, leaving sixteen meetings and sixty four copper in that teaching portion. Lin ate the meal planned for the practice day. She had not forgotten nutrition, but she was still surprised by how hungry a stopped little trace could leave her.

lark_e07_late_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_015.text: Duan wanted a midday rest before discussing the next lesson. Lin left him his room and spent the quiet interval at the market's lower wall. A man was carving little sleds to sell at the gathering even though there was no snow at that height yet. He said children could use them in the dust, which Lin thought would test the bottoms more severely than his sales pitch admitted. He handed her a rough sample and asked where it caught. She found a projecting peg. He cut it flush before putting it among the sale stock.

lark_e07_late_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_016.text: He kept the discarded peg in a jar labelled mistakes. It contained enough tiny pieces to suggest a long and busy career. Lin asked whether he planned to sell them too. He said he would when somebody proved mistakes could keep a child amused longer than a sled. She bought nothing, since her purse had other ordinary purposes. He did not take the refusal as an insult to the corrected toy. He thanked her for finding the peg and turned the next sled over to inspect its bottom before making the polished top prettier.

lark_e07_late_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_017.text: When she returned, Duan had written the next practice plan around the interrupted second movement. The plan allowed fewer attempts, not a longer effort. Recovery after each was part of the method. Lin asked whether fewer attempts could make her miss the term's exam. He said it could, and more strained attempts could do the same while damaging her route. The offered instruction did not remove that uncertainty. She read the plan through once more and accepted the actual work rather than a promise that one of the schedules guaranteed success.

lark_e07_late_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_018.text: The market gathering would begin the next day. Shan Fang had been offered a paid evening stall for repaired gloves, while Qin could take a well paid freight job at the same hour. Their household could not have both adults supervise Qin Yi's performance and accept both jobs. They had not yet chosen. Lin found the child cutting a second oversized shoe from private paper. The performance itself had become ready enough to cause the next problem: people now had to decide which real hour they could give to seeing it.

lark_e07_late_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_019.text: Lin could offer no automatic cure for that household conflict. She would be off shift during the performance but had her own accepted recovery evening after the new practice. Watching seated might be possible under that plan; running between a stall and a child was not the same task. Shan Fang asked the ordinary question instead of presuming a favor: would Lin hear the proposed arrangement tomorrow before she answered? Lin agreed to hear it. The offer had not been accepted, the stall had not been staffed, and Qin still had to decide about his freight booking.

lark_e07_late_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e07_late_020.text: That night, Lin's glove patch held without rubbing the thumb. She placed it beneath the little paper bridge above her wash basin. A diagram in the practice folder held one better interruption and one incomplete second movement. Both kinds of work had survived correction this week. She could look at either without making it speak for the other. The fifth pair had not become a certificate, and the market's next evening had not become a solved household schedule. Morning would bring the chance to do a smaller piece of each. She extinguished the lamp.
